implementation_statement: No written security policies existed; the employee handbook had one paragraph on confidentiality. POL-02 Access Control (with program governance and workforce use rules) was approved 2026-08-31 and takes effect 2026-09-01. The onboarding and termination checklist is due 2026-09-30.

provider_if_inherited: PMS vendor; productivity suite vendor; MSP
implementation_statement: The Assistant Manager creates PMS, email, and lock system accounts; the MSP creates Windows accounts. Gaps: no written approval or removal procedure; one shared Windows login on the front desk PC and one shared front desk mailbox; P07 testing found 2 former employees' PMS accounts still active; no periodic account review.
evidence: PMS user list; suite user export; HR roster

implementation_statement: The PMS enforces roles (administrator, front office, housekeeping). Housekeeping users see room status only. New PMS users get no access until a role is assigned.

Staff have no local administrator rights on the PCs (MSP policy). Gap: the default front office role includes the 'view full card number' permission, so all 5 front office users can display OTA virtual card numbers; none needs it once virtual cards are charged without display.
The PMS and the productivity suite lock accounts after repeated failed sign-ins (vendor defaults, confirmed in settings).
The back office PC and laptop lock after 10 minutes. Gap: the front desk PC signs in automatically to the shared login and never locks, because staff found it inconvenient at a 24-hour desk.

Staff reach SaaS over the internet. The MSP reaches the PCs through its remote management tool. Gaps: the lock vendor's remote support tool is always on, uses one password shared by its technicians, and has no MFA; the motel has no evidence of MFA on the MSP tool.
Guest Wi-Fi is a separate network with client isolation and internet access only (MSP, 2023). Staff Wi-Fi for the tablets joins the office network and uses a WPA2 passphrase unchanged since 2023.

Gap: no security awareness training of any kind; no guidance on phishing or on callers posing as guests, OTAs, or vendor support. Planned: training at hire and yearly from 2026-10, with a short card-handling and caller-verification module for the front desk.

The PMS records user, action, and time, including card number displays. The suite records sign-ins. Gap: firewall and PC events are not defined or collected; the firewall keeps about 7 days on the device.
evidence: PMS activity report sample; firewall log settings

control_name: Audit Record Review, Analysis, and Reporting
implementation_statement: Gap: nobody reviews the PMS activity report or sign-in logs. Planned: a weekly 20-minute review of PMS card-number displays and exports and of suite sign-in alerts, from 2026-10, recorded on a checklist.
The PMS vendor keeps activity logs for the contract term. Gap: firewall logs roll over in about 7 days; suite logs follow the plan default.
An independent security consultant assessed 14 controls on 2026-08-03 to 2026-08-05 (P07). POL-02 requires a yearly assessment.
regulatory_driver: N72-R01 (yearly SAQ validation under the merchant agreement)

implementation_statement: The MSP's tool lists the 3 PCs. Gaps: no list of the payment terminals with serial numbers, the tablets, network devices, the lock system, the CCTV recorder, or the SaaS services; no list of where card data and ID scans are stored. Planned: one-page inventory by 2026-10-31.

Gap: no contingency plan. The building hurricane checklist covers shutters and generators, not IT. Planned: a short plan from the BIA (P05) with the paper check-in kit, offline key encoding, and the hurricane steps, by 2026-12-31.

Gap: no restore test since the backup was set up in 2024; the plan has never been exercised. Planned: first restore test, including the lock database, by 2026-10-31, then quarterly; yearly tabletop with the P08 runbook.
Gap: one internet line with no failover; the terminals and the PMS both depend on it. Planned: MSP-installed cellular failover router by 2026-12-31.

The PMS vendor backs up PMS data (SOC 2 report, P09). The MSP backs up the back office PC and the suite nightly with 30 days of versions; the backup console uses MFA. Gaps: P07 testing found the lock database excluded from the backup job; no restore test; versions are not immutable.
evidence: PMS vendor SOC 2 report; backup job report (MSP)

implementation_statement: Each employee has a named PMS login. Gaps: the front desk PC uses one shared Windows login with automatic sign-in, and the front desk mailbox is shared by all clerks with one password, so actions on them cannot be tied to a person.
evidence: PMS user list; suite user export; walkthrough 2026-07-15

implementation_statement: MFA is on for PMS administrators, the two manager mailboxes, and the backup console. Gaps: no MFA for non-administrator PMS users who can display card numbers, the shared mailbox, the lock vendor's remote tool, or the firewall management login.
evidence: PMS and suite MFA settings; P07 test 2026-08-04

implementation_statement: SaaS password rules use vendor defaults. Gaps: the staff Wi-Fi passphrase and the lock vendor's shared password have never changed; the PMS minimum length is below what PCI DSS requires.
POL-03 Incident Response Policy approved 2026-08-31, effective 2026-09-01.
The P08 runbook (approved 2026-08-31) assigns the Assistant Manager as incident lead, the MSP for technical response, and the insurer's panel counsel and forensic firm. Gap: not yet tested.
evidence: P08 runbook; MSP contract; insurance policy

implementation_statement: POL-03 requires staff to report suspected incidents to the Assistant Manager within 1 hour. Gap: staff have not yet been told (training due 2026-10-31).
The P08 card compromise runbook serves as the incident response plan for this tier, with the contact card and notification matrix.

Paper with card data (crew card authorization forms) is kept in an open binder under the front desk. Gap: not locked, kept since 2021, and seen by anyone behind the desk. Planned: lock it now; no forms after the 2026-11-30 redesign; shred the binder once purged.
Paper goes through the cross-cut shredder in the back office. The MSP wipes PCs before disposal. Gaps: no record for the PC replaced in 2025; background-check reports are filed with no disposal date.

The back office behind the front desk is locked and visible from the desk; the network cabinet is in the back office. The front desk is staffed 24 hours. Keys are held by the Owner-Manager, Assistant Manager, and Night Auditor.
This SSP, approved 2026-08-31.
Workforce use rules are in POL-02 Part C (approved 2026-08-31). Gap: signed acknowledgments not yet collected.

baseline: Not in Moderate baseline (selected by tailoring)
implementation_statement: The Assistant Manager was designated Security and Privacy Lead in writing on 2026-07-01. Selected by tailoring because PCI DSS expects security roles to be assigned.
Front desk and night audit applicants are screened by a background-check company before hire.

Gap: no termination checklist; 2 former employees' PMS accounts were still active (P07). Planned: last-day checklist covering the PMS, email, lock system, shared passwords, keys, and the Wi-Fi passphrase, by 2026-09-30.
Risk assessment completed 2026-07-24 using NIST SP 800-30 Rev. 1 (P01), the first the motel has done. POL-02 requires a yearly update.
Gap: no internal scans and no external ASV scans. Planned: quarterly internal scans by the MSP and quarterly ASV scans from 2026-10, until the redesign removes the office network from scope.

AOCs on file for the PMS vendor and, since fieldwork, the gateway. Gaps: no list of service providers or responsibility matrix; no written terms with the lock vendor on remote access or incident notice; the MSP has no security commitments in its contract.

The MSP-managed firewall blocks unsolicited inbound traffic, and guest Wi-Fi is separated. Gap: the office network is flat: PCs, terminals, printer, CCTV recorder, and tablets share it, and outbound traffic is unrestricted.

provider_if_inherited: PMS vendor; payment gateway; productivity suite vendor
implementation_statement: SaaS and gateway traffic uses TLS; the terminals encrypt card data at the point of interaction. Gap: crew companies send card numbers by ordinary email.
The PMS vendor encrypts its database and vault; the laptop is encrypted. Gaps: the front desk and back office PCs are not encrypted, and card numbers sit readable in the shared mailbox.
The MSP patches the 3 PCs monthly; SaaS vendors patch their platforms. Gaps: firewall firmware is updated only when the MSP visits; the CCTV recorder firmware has never been updated.

MSP-managed antivirus runs on the 3 PCs with automatic updates. Gap: alerts reach the MSP only in business hours, and there is no behavior-based detection (EDR) on the front desk PC where card numbers are keyed.
Gap: no monitoring beyond antivirus alerts. Planned: MSP-managed EDR with after-hours alerting on the 3 PCs by 2026-12-31; suite alerts for new forwarding rules.

Gap: no retention schedule. The PMS keeps all guest profiles and about 14,000 ID scans indefinitely; card forms are kept since 2021. Planned: register data 2 years (Fla. Stat. 509.101(2)); ID scans deleted 30 days after checkout; no stored card data.
